source:
A massive storm has destroyed most of the city. Players choose how they want to live in the aftermath.

Roles
👮 Police
🚑 Paramedic
🔥 Firefighter
🛠️ Mechanic
🧑‍🌾 Farmer
🛒 Shop Owner
🏠 Builder
🦹 Criminal
👨‍👩‍👧 Civilian
Features
Build and decorate your own home.
Buy and customize vehicles.
Start businesses like cafés, gas stations, or clothing stores.
Dynamic weather (storms, floods, heatwaves).
Jobs with progression and pay.
Optional PvP zones, with safe RP areas for players who don't want combat.
Seasonal events and community missions.
What makes it different

Instead of just living a normal city life, everyone works together to rebuild the town after disasters. New events keep changing the world, giving players fresh roleplay opportunities.

It mixes the everyday roleplay of games like Brookhaven with survival and rebuilding mechanics to make the world feel more dynamic

image_prompt.text: Wide grid-aligned streets, 15 studs one-way and 30 two-way, weaving between residential streets, the commercial strip and the farms on the edge so owned vehicles turn without clipping
Clear separation between the commercial strip of cafes, gas stations, clothing stores and dealerships and the quiet residential streets
Homes, businesses and the role venues - police station, firehouse, medical center, garage - that players go inside
Dynamic environmental events layered over the shared city: storm fronts, street flooding, heatwaves

layout_placement.text: Job stations for the repeatable role loops - patient beds, fire callouts, repair bays, planting plots, shop counters

notes: Mixed: Roleplay owns the shape and preset because the prompt calls itself roleplay and centres on decorating homes and open-ended storytelling; Simulation contributes the job stations and the environmental-event hazard as options only, per its Role Sim boundary note.
P4 applies on top of P3 if each player home interior is a per-player instance.

The defining feature - the city visibly rebuilding from ruin over time, plus seasonal events - cannot be expressed. The handoff describes one static snapshot and there is no way to say which state it is in.
Optional PvP zones alongside safe roleplay areas have no option in either loaded file; they are volumes with rules attached rather than geometry.

open_questions.ask: Should the city read as mostly wrecked and being clawed back, or mostly rebuilt with damage as flavour?
How much city - a few neighbourhoods, or a sprawl with farms and outskirts? This may need the larger region frame.

coverage_missing.ask: How ruined is the city at the start?
How many neighbourhoods, and how many players share one city?
Do players build homes on empty lots, or repair pre-placed damaged houses? The rebuilding premise suggests the second, which is a different housing model.
Is the rebuilding persistent across sessions, or does the city reset?

answers.ask: Should the city read as mostly wrecked and being clawed back, or mostly rebuilt with damage as flavour?
answers.answer: The city should read as mostly wrecked and actively being clawed back after the storm, with clear damage, debris, and incomplete rebuilding throughout.

answers.ask: How much city - a few neighbourhoods, or a sprawl with farms and outskirts? This may need the larger region frame.
answers.answer: Use a few compact neighbourhoods with a small farm/outskirts area, keeping the first map focused on a playable rebuilding community rather than a large sprawl.
